findings.description: All calls to the same decorated function now share one statistics dict, and each call clears it at entry. Overlapping calls from different threads corrupt each other's counters, and the earlier call's statistics are wiped mid-run.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two threads (or overlapping invocations) call the same @retry-decorated function at once. Mechanism: the second call runs stats.clear() and then both copies write into the same dict, where previously each call got its own dict via copy.statistics. Impact: statistics read from wrapped_f.statistics or the first call's retry state show mixed or reset attempt counts, a silent wrong result. Retry decisions use per-call retry state, so the damage is limited to reported statistics.

findings.description: The asyncio wrapper has the same shared-dict problem: stats.clear() runs on every entry, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated coroutine function reset and interleave each other's statistics.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two tasks await the same @retry-decorated async function concurrently via asyncio.gather. Mechanism: the second invocation clears the shared dict and both copies update it, so the earlier invocation's statistics are reset and mixed with the later one's. Impact: observed attempt_number and statistics for each call are wrong, a silent wrong result, though retry control flow is unaffected.
